transcript.content: Hello, welcome. Please have a seat. What brings you in today?
I came in because I just can’t shake this heavy, hopeless feeling. It feels like everything I’d built back up after my divorce has collapsed, and I’m just… sitting under all of it.
How long have you been feeling this way?
About a month now. It started around when the financial mess from the divorce really hit, and since then it’s just been hanging over me.
Have you lost interest or felt no pleasure in activities that you used to enjoy, like hobbies, work, or spending time with friends or family?

I’m not really sure. I mean, I haven’t paid close attention to that specifically. I know I’ve been feeling really low, but I can’t say clearly whether it’s that I don’t enjoy things or that I just haven’t been doing much.
Looking back at the last month, have you found that you don’t take pleasure or feel interested in things you used to enjoy, like hobbies, work, or time with friends or family?

I’m still not totally sure how to separate that out. I haven’t really been doing much of anything lately, so it’s hard to tell if I don’t enjoy things or if I just haven’t had the energy or focus to try.
Even if you haven’t been doing much lately, can you recall if you still would have enjoyed those things if you had done them?
I honestly don’t know. I can imagine some of it might have been okay, but I haven’t really felt clear enough to tell whether I’d actually enjoy it or just be going through the motions.
Looking back, do you think you would still enjoy the things you used to, like hobbies or time with friends, or has that enjoyment gone away completely?

I really can’t say for sure. It doesn’t feel like I can clearly tell whether the enjoyment is gone, or whether I just haven’t been in a place to try those things and notice. I know I haven’t been doing much, but I don’t want to say it’s completely gone if I’m not sure.
Have you noticed any change in how you feel about the things you used to enjoy, like hobbies or time with friends, even if you haven’t been doing them much lately?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed a clear change exactly, because I haven’t been doing those things much. It’s hard for me to tell if I’d feel different about them or not.
Even if you haven’t been doing much lately, have you noticed any decrease in how much you care about or look forward to the things you used to enjoy, like hobbies or time with friends?

I’m not sure I’ve noticed that clearly. I haven’t really been looking forward to much, but I also haven’t been trying to plan or do those things, so it’s hard to tell if I care less or if I’m just kind of not in that mindset right now.
Looking back, have you felt less of a desire or longing to do the things you used to enjoy, even if you haven’t actually been doing them lately?

I’m not sure I can separate that out. I haven’t really felt a strong pull to do those things, but I don’t know if that means the desire is actually less, or if I’ve just been kind of not thinking about them much.
Looking back, have you felt less interested in the things you used to enjoy, even if you haven’t actually been doing them lately?
I don’t know. I haven’t really noticed a clear drop in interest, but I also haven’t been doing much of those things, so it’s hard for me to say for sure.
Looking back, have you felt less interested in the things you used to enjoy, even if you haven’t actually been doing them lately?
I honestly don’t know. I haven’t been thinking about those things much, so I can’t really tell if I’m less interested or if I’m just not engaging with them right now.
Looking back, have you felt less interested in the things you used to enjoy, even if you haven’t actually been doing them lately?
I’m still not really sure. I haven’t felt a clear “yes, I don’t care about that anymore,” but I also haven’t been drawn to those things much lately, so it’s hard for me to tell.

Looking back, can you recall if you used to look forward to things like hobbies or time with friends, and if that sense of anticipation or enjoyment feels different now, even if you haven’t been doing those things lately?

I’m not sure. I can remember that I used to look forward to things, but right now it’s kind of hard to tell if that feeling is actually gone or if I just haven’t been in the mindset to think about it. I haven’t really noticed it clearly one way or the other.
Looking back, can you clearly say that you’ve felt less pleasure or enjoyment in the things you used to enjoy, even if you haven’t been doing them much lately?
No, I can’t clearly say that. I know I haven’t been doing those things much, but I can’t tell if I’d enjoy them less or if I just haven’t really been thinking about them.

Looking back, even if you haven’t been doing much lately, can you say for sure that you’ve felt less pleasure or enjoyment when you did engage in activities you used to like, such as hobbies or time with friends?

I don’t think I can say that for sure. The few times I’ve done something, I wasn’t really paying close enough attention to whether I enjoyed it less. I just know I haven’t been doing much, so it’s hard to separate that out.

Looking back, even if you haven’t been doing much lately, can you say that you’ve felt less pleasure or enjoyment in activities you used to like, such as hobbies or time with friends, just based on your thoughts or feelings about them?

I still don’t think I can say that based on my thoughts either. I haven’t really been checking in with myself that way. I know I haven’t been doing much, but I can’t clearly say, “yeah, I’d enjoy it less.”

Looking back, even if you haven’t been doing much lately, can you say that you’ve felt less pleasure or enjoyment in the idea of activities you used to like, such as hobbies or time with friends, just based on how you feel inside?

I’m still not sure. Like, when I think about those things, I don’t get a clear feeling one way or the other. It’s more like I haven’t really been focused on wanting to do them, but I can’t honestly say the idea of them feels less enjoyable.
Looking back, even if you haven’t been doing them much lately, do you feel like you’ve genuinely cared less about the things you used to enjoy, such as hobbies or time with friends?
I’m not really sure. I can tell I haven’t been doing those things much, but I don’t know if that means I care less about them. I haven’t noticed a clear feeling like that.

Looking back, even if you haven’t been doing them much lately, do you feel like you’ve had a clear decrease in how much you care about or feel motivated to engage in the things you used to enjoy, such as hobbies or time with friends?

I don’t think I can say there’s been a clear decrease. I know I haven’t been engaging much, but when you ask if I care less or feel less motivated in a clear way… I’m not sure. I haven’t really noticed it that specifically.

Looking back, even if you haven’t been doing them much lately, have you noticed that the thought of doing the things you used to enjoy, like hobbies or time with friends, feels less appealing or motivating to you now than before this period started?

I don’t know that I’ve noticed that clearly. Like, I haven’t been doing those things much, but when I picture them, I can’t really tell if they feel less appealing than before. It’s more like I just haven’t been thinking about them much.
